prepared_by: Processing, transcription and checks were carried out in November 2026 with an AI assistant (Claude, made by Anthropic) working at the direction of the ShakeReady project lead. Values taken from published documents were transcribed and then compared against those documents by script.

nbi-2025-ca.title: National Bridge Inventory, 2025, California, comma-delimited file (CA25.txt)
nbi-2025-ca.publisher: Federal Highway Administration, U.S. Department of Transportation
nbi-2025-ca.note: FHWA's download page gives 25,975 highway bridges for California in 2025 and states that 2025 was the last year submitted in the Coding Guide format. A copy of the file is kept in the project's archive.

hazus-6.1.title: Hazus Earthquake Model Technical Manual, Hazus 6.1, July 2024
hazus-6.1.note: Section 7.1, Highway Transportation System: Tables 7-1, 7-2 and 7-6, Equations 7-1 to 7-4, and the worked example in Section 7.1.6.2. The manual credits Basoz and Mander (1999) for the theory behind the bridge damage functions.

datasets.title: NBI bridges, California, 2025
processing: Read the comma-delimited file (single quote as text qualifier). All 25,975 records are of record type 1, the route carried on the structure, and all are kept.
Convert latitude (Item 16) and longitude (Item 17) from packed degrees, minutes and seconds to decimal degrees; west longitude is made negative.
Decode material and design codes (Item 43 for the main spans, Item 44 for approach spans) and county codes (Item 3) to names.
Carry over year built and reconstructed, lanes, traffic, span counts and lengths, skew and condition ratings as recorded.
Assign each record its HAZUS highway bridge class (see the fragility set).

Write one GeoJSON point per placemark with every attribute carried over unchanged.

datasets.title: HAZUS highway bridges (fragility set)
processing: Transcribe the classification scheme (Table 7-1), the K3D coefficients (Table 7-2) and the median values (Table 7-6).
Implement Equations 7-1 to 7-4 and the damage algorithm for ground shaking.
Record every choice made where the manual is silent or inconsistent (decisions HZ-01 to HZ-11).

inventory_decisions.choice: All records in the FHWA highway-bridge file are included.
inventory_decisions.basis: The file holds only record type 1 (the route carried on the structure), so no record is a duplicate view of another.

inventory_decisions.choice: A record is placed on the map only if its coordinates fall inside a bounding box around California (32.0 to 42.1 north, 124.6 to 114.0 west). Other records are listed in the CSV without coordinates.
inventory_decisions.basis: Guards against missing or mistyped coordinates in the source.

inventory_decisions.choice: When a bridge has no approach spans (Item 46 is zero), its approach material and design are shown as None.
inventory_decisions.basis: The source codes these as 'other', which reads as if a material were present.

inventory_decisions.choice: A value of zero in Item 106 means the bridge has not been reconstructed.

inventory_decisions.topic: Names of what a bridge carries and crosses
inventory_decisions.choice: Item 7 (facility carried) and Item 6A (feature intersected) are shown as recorded, with repeated spaces removed.
inventory_decisions.basis: No spelling or capitalization is changed, so the text can be matched to the source.

inventory_decisions.choice: Every attribute in the original files is carried over unchanged.
inventory_decisions.basis: The building layers are an archive of the original team's work, not a new compilation.

inventory_decisions.topic: Positions of the six non-ductile buildings
inventory_decisions.choice: Their positions are taken from the Latitude and Longitude attributes in the file (for example '34.0488 N' and '118.2595 W'), with west made negative.
inventory_decisions.basis: The original file stored only street addresses for these six, which the original map service located on the fly.

inventory_decisions.choice: The bridge data from the original site (about 2016, 25,431 records) is archived and no longer shown.
inventory_decisions.basis: Replaced by the 2025 file. The earlier snapshot lacked span counts and condition ratings, and 60 of its records had no coordinates.

verification.result: 25,975 records read, equal to the count FHWA publishes for California in 2025.
For the 24,415 bridges present in both the 2025 file and the earlier snapshot, 95% of locations agree to within about 6 meters and 99% have the same year built.
The longest span in the file is the Golden Gate Bridge at 1,280.2 m, the correct value.
A script compared the transcribed values with the text of the manual: all 28 sets of medians match, as do the K3D equation, I-shape value and design era of the 27 classes that have them.
The classification function returns the class given in every row of Table 7-1.
Reproduced: class HWB17, K3D = 1.125, and damage-state probabilities 0.183, 0.205, 0.165, 0.255, 0.192 against the manual's rounded 0.18, 0.20, 0.16, 0.26, 0.20.

verification.check: The map against the reference code
verification.result: For 425 sampled bridges, covering every class present, the adjusted medians computed in the browser equal those of the reference code to rounding error.
Each filter tested returns the same number of bridges as an independent count from the data file.

verification.check: Damage calculation against an independent implementation
verification.result: The table produced by the map was compared with the one produced by separate reference code (tools/damage_reference.py), using made-up test layers that are not published: a hazard map at two probability levels and a scenario. For all 25,974 bridges the two tables are identical, character for character.
The expected counts shown on the map equal the sums from the reference table. A table downloaded with a county filter applied contains exactly the reference rows for that county.

Seven real USGS ShakeMap grid files (shortened samples from the OpenQuake engine's test data, three versions of the ShakeMap software, both unit spellings): every row read lands on the right grid node with the right value. For a full grid in the same layout, all 81,993 values match the source after conversion from percent of g, zipped or not.
A table in cm/s² with its own column names and rows in random order is placed correctly on its grid and converted to g.

verification.check: An SR-HazardMaker layer on the map
verification.result: A layer made in SR-HazardMaker and opened on the map gives a damage table identical, for all 25,974 bridges, to the reference code run on the same layer file. The checksum shown equals the file's.

verification.check: SR-HazardMaker: browser and command line against each other
verification.result: The tool's own test suite (21 tests, run automatically on every change) builds the same inputs with the Python converters and with the browser converters and requires the same layer from both: USGS-style tables given separately, in an archive and in a ZIP64 archive; ShakeMap grids with either unit spelling, any field order and any row order, zipped or not; and a plain table in cm/s². Reading a value at a point must agree exactly at 4,000 random points. On this site, a 290 MB archive gave the same layer, with only the three tables needed read from it.

verification.check: A layer file opened on the map
verification.result: A layer file opened from the computer on the map gives the same damage table as the reference code for all 25,974 bridges. A file that is not a layer is refused.

limits: The HAZUS curves describe classes of bridges, not individual structures. They suit screening an inventory, not conclusions about one bridge.
The NBI does not record seismic retrofits, so retrofitted bridges are treated as built (decision HZ-10).
Culverts are in the inventory and are given bridge curves, which fit them poorly (decision HZ-09).
Only ground shaking is considered. Liquefaction, landslide and fault-rupture displacement are not (decision HZ-08).
NBI values are as submitted by the owning agencies. No value has been corrected.
The building layers date from 2017 and have not been updated.

damage_decisions.choice: The value at an asset is found by bilinear interpolation between the four grid nodes around it.
damage_decisions.basis: Hazard layers are grids; assets lie between nodes. Bilinear interpolation is the simplest method that varies smoothly and adds no information of its own.

damage_decisions.choice: A node without a value is left out and the remaining nodes' weights are rescaled. An asset outside the grid, or with no valid node around it, gets no estimate and is listed with blank cells.
damage_decisions.basis: Avoids inventing ground motion where the layer has none, such as offshore or beyond the edge of a scenario.

damage_decisions.choice: A layer's values are used as published. No further adjustment is made for the soil at each asset.
damage_decisions.basis: Each layer states the ground condition its values assume. If that is a uniform reference condition, shaking on softer ground is understated, and so is damage there.

damage_decisions.choice: The probability of reaching a more severe state is not allowed to exceed that of a milder one.
damage_decisions.basis: After the manual's adjustments, the median for a more severe state can fall at or below that of a milder one (for example where a class has equal medians for two states). Without this rule a state could receive a negative probability.

damage_decisions.topic: Results from a probabilistic hazard map
damage_decisions.choice: Each asset is evaluated at its own site's ground motion for the chosen probability level.
damage_decisions.basis: A hazard map does not describe one earthquake: its values would not all occur together. Results are therefore per asset. Totals across assets are shown as a description of the inventory, not as the loss from an event.

damage_decisions.topic: Expected number in each damage state
damage_decisions.choice: The expected number of assets in a state is the sum of their probabilities of being in that state.
damage_decisions.basis: Standard for expected counts. It carries the caution in DMG-05 when the layer is probabilistic.

damage_decisions.choice: The state with the highest probability. A tie goes to the milder state.
damage_decisions.basis: A single label per asset is useful on a map, but it hides the spread. The five probabilities are always given alongside it.

damage_decisions.choice: Values are given to four decimal places, an exact half rounded up. Coordinates are given to five.
damage_decisions.basis: Stated so that the table can be reproduced exactly by the reference code.

hazard_decisions.choice: Ground motions are stored in thousandths of g. An exact half rounds up.
hazard_decisions.basis: 0.001 g is finer than any of the sources warrant, and whole numbers keep the files small. The rounding rule is stated so that the two converters, in the browser and on the command line, give identical files.

hazard_decisions.topic: Area kept from the USGS hazard model
hazard_decisions.choice: USGS hazard-model tables are cropped to latitude 32.0 to 42.5 north and longitude 125.0 to 113.5 west.
hazard_decisions.basis: The national files cover the conterminous United States. The crop keeps California with a margin, so that every structure has grid nodes on all sides.

hazard_decisions.choice: Each measure is converted to g from the units the file states for it. Percent of g is recognized in both spellings found in USGS files, 'pctg' and '%g'. A file with any other unit is refused.
hazard_decisions.basis: USGS changed the spelling between software versions. Reading the unit from the file avoids assuming it.

hazard_decisions.choice: The whole grid is kept. The spacing is taken as the grid's extent divided by its number of intervals, and each row is placed by its own coordinates.
hazard_decisions.basis: The file's stated spacing is rounded to four decimals, which would drift across several hundred nodes. Placing rows by their coordinates does not depend on the order in which the file lists them.

hazard_decisions.choice: A ShakeMap layer is labeled site-specific.
hazard_decisions.basis: ShakeMap estimates the shaking at the ground surface using its own map of ground conditions, so no uniform reference condition applies.

hazard_decisions.choice: The points must form an evenly spaced grid in latitude and longitude. Accelerations in cm/s² or m/s² are converted with g = 9.80665 m/s².
hazard_decisions.basis: Scattered points would need a gridding method, which is a modeling choice that belongs to whoever produced the ground motions.

hazard_decisions.choice: SR-HazardMaker will not build a layer without a title, a ground condition, a source title, a publisher or author, and a date. It fills these in only when the file itself identifies them.
hazard_decisions.basis: A layer whose origin is unknown cannot support a traceable result.

hazard_decisions.choice: A layer made with SR-HazardMaker, or opened from a file on the user's computer, can be used on the map without being published. It is marked as the user's own, and any damage table made from it states that it is not part of the ShakeReady repository and gives its checksum.
hazard_decisions.basis: Lets people work with their own ground motions at once, without letting an unreviewed layer pass for a published one.

hazard_decisions.choice: SR-HazardMaker is kept in its own repository. This site copies a tagged release of it without changes and records the release, the commit and a checksum of each copied file.
hazard_decisions.basis: A single source for the converters, in the browser and on the command line, so that the public tool and the one this site uses cannot drift apart.
